definitions.explanation: Both of one's arms. Used to emphasize that both arms are involved in an action.
Two people who serve as one's most trusted and capable assistants. A figurative extension from the literal meaning.

examples.japanese: {両腕|りょううで}で{抱|かか}える。
{両腕|りょううで}を{広|ひろ}げて{迎|むか}えた。
examples.english: I spread both arms wide to welcome them.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもを{両腕|りょううで}でしっかり{抱|だ}きしめた。
examples.english: I held the child tightly with both arms.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}の{両腕|りょううで}として{会社|かいしゃ}を{支|ささ}えている。
examples.english: They support the company as the president's right-hand men.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{監督|かんとく}の{両腕|りょううで}と{呼|よ}ばれるコーチだ。
examples.english: He is a coach known as the manager's right-hand man.

examples.japanese: {優秀|ゆうしゅう}な{二人|ふたり}の{部下|ぶか}を{両腕|りょううで}に、{新|あたら}しいプロジェクトを{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: With two excellent subordinates as my right-hand men, I started a new project.

notes:
{両腕|りょううで} literally means "both arms" but also has a figurative meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {両腕|りょううで}で{抱|かか}える (to hold in both arms)
- {両腕|りょううで}を{広|ひろ}げる (to spread both arms)
- {両腕|りょううで}を{組|く}む (to fold both arms)

SIMILAR COMPOUNDS:
- {両手|りょうて} (both hands)
- {両足|りょうあし} (both legs)
- {片腕|かたうで} (one arm; one's right-hand man — singular)
